instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched Bonsai/Blender graphical user interface. Do not open Terminal or a shell; do not use the Blender Python console, Text editor scripts, Python, IfcOpenShell, shell commands, or any helper script/macro to directly generate or edit the deliverable files. Use only Bonsai/Blender native GUI tools, panels, menus, dialogs, and built-in save/export commands. Open the provided init.ifc model in Bonsai and use init_plan.png as the plan reference. Correct the spatial containment so ground-floor elements belong to the Ground Floor storey and first-floor elements belong to the First Floor storey, then save the completed IFC4 model as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc using Bonsai's graphical save/export controls. The result should keep one project, one site, and one building, with exactly two building storeys named Ground Floor and First Floor. It should contain exactly eight IfcWall elements and exactly two IfcSlab elements, with no IfcBuildingElementProxy or IfcFurniture objects. Through IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure relationships, Ground Floor should contain exactly GF South Wall, GF North Wall, GF West Wall, GF East Wall, and GF Slab. First Floor should contain exactly FF South Wall, FF North Wall, FF West Wall, FF East Wall, and FF Slab. Do not create a CSV schedule or separate report file; the required storey assignment must be represented directly in result.ifc. Other non-required IFC metadata may vary as long as the saved model satisfies these stated GUI-created IFC requirements.
